Today's big story
Risk-off Monday: U.S. strikes on Iran and a hawkish Fed push crypto lower — but Bitcoin holds near $79K after a 24% August.
The tape turned defensive to close August: the first U.S. strikes against Iran in weeks sent oil higher and stocks lower, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole message — the Fed’s duty is lower prices — has markets bracing for hikes rather than cuts. Every major index closed red and crypto followed: BTC $78,675 (-0.2%), ETH $2,474, SOL -3.0%. The context matters more than the day: Bitcoin still ended August up roughly 24%, its best monthly stretch since early 2023, on a run that included Coinbase widening BTC-backed mortgages and the SEC sending its custody proposal to the White House. A red Monday inside a green month — positioning, not conviction, moved today.
Bitcoin Rates Geopolitics

SKR nearly doubled (+94.2% to $0.03) with $385M traded — 1.8x its market cap turning over in a day. The token behind Solana Mobile’s $500 Seeker phone caught two catalysts at once: the close of the “Seeker Summer” rewards season (over 100M SKR earned across 16 apps, 300k+ badges claimed) and a limited retail push offering Seeker discounts payable in stablecoins or SKR via Solana Pay. Reward-season spikes are event-driven by construction — they fade as fast as the calendar that made them. Illustrative only, not advice.
01 — Fintech pulse
Warsh resets the rate conversation — while institutions keep buying the rails.
The macro backdrop shifted this weekend: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh used Jackson Hole to reiterate that the Fed’s duty is lower prices, and renewed U.S.–Iran hostilities pushed oil higher — together raising expectations that the next move on rates is up, not down. Risk assets sold the message; crypto’s reaction was notably muted for an asset class that used to trade as pure beta.
Under the headlines, institutional plumbing keeps getting built: Third Point disclosed a $151.8M Hut 8 position plus new stakes in Riot, Core Scientific, and Applied Digital — the miners-as-AI-infrastructure trade going mainstream — while August’s SEC custody proposal continues through White House review. Hawkish tape, dovish plumbing. For builders the lesson holds: rails and custody are the moat.
TRADE ON SWOP →
02 — From the Journal
ERC-8196 in production: how Swop polices its trading agent
New on the Swop Journal today: ERC-8196 — now Final on Ethereum — standardizes wallets that only execute an AI agent’s transaction with proof it complies with a policy the owner defined. Swop’s Goldman trading agent runs under an ERC-8196-inspired policy layer in production: versioned per-vault policies, EIP-712 owner signatures to expand authority, and a hash-chained audit log for every enforcement decision. One rule sits above all of it — exits are never blocked.
Also new: what “gasless crypto wallet” actually means — who really pays the fee, and what to check before trusting the claim.
READ THE POST →
03 — Day ahead
What to watch — macro, courts, and tonight's board.
📅 Macro Calendar
• Tue 10:00 ET — ISM Manufacturing PMI — first read on September’s tape
• Wed 14:00 ET — Fed Beige Book + JOLTS — the labor-market picture Warsh says he’s watching
• Fri 8:30 ET — August jobs report — the week’s main event; after Jackson Hole, a hot print prices in hikes
• Ongoing — Oil and the Iran headlines — the fastest channel from geopolitics to rate expectations
⚖ Court Watch
• SEC custody rule — the adviser custody rewrite for digital assets remains in White House review — institutional self-custody plumbing
• Regulation Crypto Assets — comment window still open on the SEC’s first purpose-built crypto framework
• Agent standards — ERC-8196 (agent-authenticated wallets) is Final; the compliance conversation moves from courtrooms to code — today’s Journal post covers it
🎯 Tonight's Games · Swop Predictions vs. the Books
• US Open · Day 2 (all day, ESPN) — first round rolls on; Sabalenka’s three-peat bid and top seed Zverev headline — tournament futures are where prediction-market prices drift furthest from the books
• Mets @ Rays · Mariners @ Red Sox (MLB · tonight) — a 12-game pennant-race slate; September call-up season is when thin books lag lineup news the most
• Giants @ Braves (6:05 ET) — wild-card pressure game on a quiet holiday-week Monday
